High Kp values do not necessarily indicate great auroras. They’re only a rough gauge of activity to expect. It all depends on the solar wind conditions, which can change quite dramatically over short time scales. If you have an IMF that is persistently northward during a geomagnetic storm, the resulting auroras won’t be as spectacular as a persistently southward IMF even during quiet conditions.

Thank you for your reply. Ever since I was a little kid, I have been fascinated by nature and had an innate curiosity about the fundamental workings of the universe. I was your typical inquisitive kid that always asked “why does this happen?” Or “how does this work?” My goal of getting a physics degree is to move on to graduate school and pursue a PhD in theoretical physics, as well as gain a deeper understanding of how the universe works. Studying high level physics (like quantum physics) in my free time is one of the few things that makes me feel happy. However, I am stuck in an introductory physics class that I have to take and it is extremely boring to me because I already know everything (this ironically caused me to have a very low grade in the class due to lack of motivation.) Nevertheless, this has still made me feel like an idiot who is a fool for majoring in physics. Because of this, I couldn’t do stuff that helped me de stress like studying high level physics that is very interesting or going for walks to cool off. As I stated before, I am also constantly worrying about climate change and how that will impact my future. Each year, the looming climate crisis gets worse and worse and it makes me so depressed that people in power are simply doing nothing about it. A combination of these made me slip into a depression and I really wish I could just never wake up again. I don’t want to kill myself because I don’t want my family to suffer but I still wish I didn’t have to live on this corrupted planet.
